facts.statement: An authorized insurer holds a current certificate of authority from the commissioner; an unauthorized insurer does not.
facts.quote: An “unauthorized insurer” is an insurer not so authorized.

items.stem: An insurer formed in Delaware sells life policies by mail to New Jersey residents, but it has never received a certificate of authority from the New Jersey commissioner. In New Jersey it is:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:17-11 defines an authorized insurer as one holding a current certificate of authority from the commissioner; any other insurer is unauthorized.
items.retired: Stem states the lack of a certificate, which names the answer; no rewrite avoids it.

facts.statement: No one may solicit, negotiate or effect insurance, deliver a policy, collect premiums or otherwise transact insurance in New Jersey unless specifically authorized.
facts.quote: unless specifically authorized under the laws of this State

items.stem: A person with no New Jersey license or authorization collects premium payments from New Jersey residents on behalf of an out-of-state insurer, but never solicits or sells a policy. Under New Jersey law, this is:
options: Allowed, since he did not solicit or sell
Allowed, if the insurer is licensed in its home state
Prohibited, since receiving premiums is transacting insurance
Prohibited only if the policies are life policies
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:17-13(a)-(b) bars anyone, unless specifically authorized, from soliciting, negotiating, delivering a policy, receiving any premium, or otherwise transacting insurance in New Jersey.

facts.statement: Every insurer must file a sworn annual financial statement with the commissioner by March 1, and quarterly statements within 45 days after each quarter.
facts.quote: on or before March 1, file with the commissioner a statement subscribed and sworn to

items.stem: Every insurer transacting business in New Jersey must file its sworn annual financial statement with the commissioner by:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:21-1(a) requires the annual statement, showing condition as of December 31, to be filed on or before March 1. Quarterly statements are due within 45 days after each quarter.
